errors: The machine constraint is misread. The text says the production decision (binary) is multiplied by -71.8 or -73.1, which gives x - cap*y + startup_time*s <= 0. The model multiplies the continuous quantity x by the coefficient instead, giving (1-71.8)x + 6.34*s <= 0. This removes the capacity limit on x and no longer reduces capacity when a startup occurs.

No startup is required in period 0. Production in period 0 (y[0,0,0] and y[1,1,0]) incurs no startup cost, since startup_link only covers t>=1. The usual reading treats the machine as initially off, so a startup is needed whenever production begins in period 0. The model therefore likely underestimates cost by about 2*79.19.

errors: The machine constraint has a sign error. prod_rate is already stored as a negative number (-71.8, -73.1), and the code applies another negation, so the coefficient on x becomes +71.8 or +73.1. With the extra +x term and the nonnegative startup term, every x is forced to 0. No production is possible, and the solution is all backlog (objective 2605).

The constraint never links x to the production binary y, so x has no capacity bound tied to y. The stated constraint multiplies the rate by the production decision (the binary), giving -rate*y + startup_time*s + x <= 0, i.e. x <= rate*y - startup_time*s. The code multiplies the rate by x instead, which is not that constraint.
As a result the reported solution is degenerate: no production, no setups, no startups, and large backlogs. The intended optimum would produce to meet demand and would have a very different cost.
